description:
UAT records skipped and unreachable cells, but the release report's candidate
counts do not fully represent them - so a release can look more complete than it
is. When skipped/unreachable cells silently shrink the denominator, a "passed N
of N" summary reads as full coverage when some cells never actually ran. That is
a release-evidence integrity problem, not a cosmetic one: the report is the
artifact a release decision is made against.

Audit the UAT report/validate accounting so skipped and unreachable cells appear
as explicit, reconciling denominators (e.g. passed / attempted / total-defined,
with skipped and unreachable broken out), and a non-zero unreachable count is
surfaced loudly in the summary rather than quietly absorbed.

preserves.behavior: Existing UAT report consumers (TSV columns) keep working; add columns/lines rather than renaming existing ones unless necessary.
Pass/fail classification of cells is unchanged; only the denominator representation and visibility change.

develop @ cb49cecf5) so the defect is pinned before the fix. This re-validates
the description's claim rather than assuming it.
